messages.author: 9e5a298f3356dbd4
messages.subject: Interactive filter for plot
parts:
I currently have some data for which I'd love to be able to add an interactive multiple checkbox option that lets the user select which area of the body they want to view data from. At the moment it looks like this:

    areas_data %>%
    ggvis(~Bacilli, ~Actinobacteria) %>%
    filter(area %in% c("Skin", "Oral", "Gut") ) %>%
    layer_points( fill = ~area, size := 50, opacity := 0.5)

I can't figure out how to change the filter line so that it will interactively change the data you're viewing. I've tried inserting input_checkboxgroup into the filter line, but keep receiving an error about how the comparison is only possible for atomic and list types. I've tried a lot of different variants of the line, an example being:

    filter(area %in% input_checkboxgroup(c("Skin" = "Skin", "Oral" = "Oral", "Gut" = "Gut") ) ) %>%

Thanks!

messages.author: 912329a6ad1a6995
messages.subject: Re: Interactive filter for plot
parts:
Hi,

I don't have a solution, but maybe I can try to move the ball forward with a reproducible example using the cocaine dataset.

Does this approximate your issue?

library(ggvis)

upper_midwest <- c("Iowa" = IA", "Minnesota" = "MN", "Wisconsin" = "WI")

# works OK
cocaine %>%
  ggvis(~potency, ~price) %>%
  filter(state %in% upper_midwest) %>%
  layer_points(fill = ~state, size := 50, opacity := 0.5)

# error
cocaine %>%  
  ggvis(~potency, ~price) %>%
  filter(state %in% input_checkboxgroup(choices = upper_midwest)) %>%
  layer_points(fill = ~state, size := 50, opacity := 0.5)

messages.author: 912329a6ad1a6995
messages.subject: Re: Interactive filter for plot
parts:
Here's a shiny version that works for me. 

It's ugly. 

Maybe it can help shake something loose.

library(ggvis)
library(shiny)
library(dplyr)

shinyApp(
  ui = 
    fluidPage(
      fluidRow(
        column(
          width = 3,
          checkboxGroupInput(
            "state",
            label = "State",
            choices = upper_midwest,
            selected = "IA"
          )
        ),
        column(
          width = 9,
          ggvisOutput("cocaine_state")
        )
      )  
    ),
  
  server = function(input, output, session){

   
    rct_cocaine <- reactive({
      cocaine %>% filter((state %in% input$state))  
    })

    observe(print(input$state))
    observe(glimpse(rct_cocaine()))
    
    # works OK
    rct_cocaine %>%
      ggvis(~potency, ~price) %>%
      layer_points(fill = ~state, size := 50, opacity := 0.5) %>%
      bind_shiny("cocaine_state")
    
  }  
)

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Interactive filter for plot
parts:
I made two changes:

* Both dplyr and ggvis using non-standard evaluation in slightly
different ways, so filter() needs a bit of a hint that
input_checkboxgroup() should be evaluated different. Surround it in
eval() to force it to be evaluated eagerly (this is documented in
filter.ggvis)

* Currently the default selected value is NULL, which selects no
values, and hence ggvis tries to plot an empty data frame and fails
(this is a bug). So you also need to check at least one group by
default. I've filed an issue about this :
https://github.com/rstudio/ggvis/issues/272

Hadley
